extractedText: Oil Near $100, U.S. Yields at 5% Put KOSPI's 7,000 Line to the TestKOSPI Rises 3.3% Last Week, Retakes 7,000 After 33 Sessions Chip Stocks Lead Index on Samsung, SK hynix and AI Hopes Brent Tops $100 While U.S. 10-Year Yield Climbs to 4.97% Fed's Sept. 15-16 Rate Decision Looms as Biggest Variable Brokerages See Ceiling at 7,500 and Floor in Mid-6,000sFinance|Published 2026.09.13. 07:00:05|By Shin Ji-minjimnn@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAAScreens at Hana Bank's dealing room in Seoul's Jung-gu district display the Kospi and other indexes on Nov. 11. The Kospi closed at 6,909.91, down 124.01 points, or 1.76%, from the previous session, while the Kosdaq ended at 820.64, down 16.28 points, or 1.95%. Yonhap NewsThe KOSPI reclaimed the 7,000 line for the first time in a month and a half before slipping back to the 6,900s. Expectations that OpenAI's release of GPT-6, called Astra, would expand demand for memory chips lifted Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK hynix (000660.KS), but the rally proved short-lived as international oil prices and U.S. Treasury yields climbed again. With the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting scheduled for next week, the gathering is expected to be a watershed for whether the index can hold above 7,000.The KOSPI closed at 6,909.91 on the 11th, up 3.33% from 6,687.21 at the end of the previous week, according to the Korea Exchange (KRX) on the 13th. The index jumped 4.61% on the 7th to 6,995.39, fell 0.58% on the 8th, then rose 1.40% on the 9th to 7,051.64, closing above 7,000 for the first time in 33 trading sessions. It then gave up that level with consecutive declines of 0.25% on the 10th and 1.76% on the 11th.Chips drove the index this week. OpenAI's unveiling of its next-generation AI model Astra, hopes for expanded investment in AI data centers, and the prospect of more long-term supply agreements (LTAs) between hyperscalers and memory makers all converged. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix surged 5.68% and 8.26%, respectively, on the 7th. Analysts read the gains as reflecting growing expectations that memory demand could rise further if artificial general intelligence (AGI) spreads.Retail investors, however, kept taking profits. Through the 9th, individuals sold a net 16.8356 trillion won ($12.1 billion) over five consecutive trading sessions. Net selling on the 7th alone reached 6.8274 trillion won, the second-largest daily figure on record. The selling is read as retail investors who bought during the June-July slump unloading shares near the 7,000 line to recover their principal.Back Above 7,000, but Oil and Yield Pressures ReturnThe U.S. Marine Corps' 31st Marine Expeditionary Unit uses a helicopter in April to search the civilian vessel Blue Star 3, which was heading for an Iranian port through a counter-blockade of the Strait of Hormuz in the Arabian Sea. Screenshot from video provided by U.S. Central Command.Overheating inside the market has cooled considerably from June and July. Not once this month has a sidecar been triggered on either the KOSPI or the KOSDAQ. The KOSPI 200 Volatility Index (VKOSPI) fell to 46.28 on the 11th, about half the 96.94 recorded on June 29. Reduced trading in single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) is also seen as having helped curb extreme price swings.The problem is macro. As the war in Iran escalated again, Brent crude has risen about 30% in the second half of the year to top $100 a barrel, and U.S. Treasury yields have jumped as well. The U.S. 10-year yield rose as high as 4.97% during trading on the 11th, approaching the 4.99% peak of October 2023. A move above 5% would be a level that could weigh heavily on stock market sentiment.Market attention is focused on the FOMC meeting on the 15th and 16th. Brokerages say an unexpected rate increase cannot be ruled out, given inflation pressure from higher oil prices and solid U.S. employment data. The federal funds futures market has priced the odds of a rate increase this month at about 60%, and the probability of at least one increase this year at about 85%. Even if the Fed holds rates, a hawkish message signaling a fourth-quarter increase would weigh on equities.Chips as a Shield: Ceiling of 7,500, Floor in the Mid-6,000sSamsung Electronics and SK hynix. Yonhap NewsEven so, the industry leans toward the view that chips could support the KOSPI's downside. SK Securities noted that when oil prices and Treasury yields rose together in March through May of this year, sectors tied to AI capital expenditure, such as IT hardware and semiconductors, actually strengthened in Korea. "The less attractive other sectors such as consumer discretionary and energy become as investments under high oil prices and high interest rates, the more funds can concentrate again on semiconductors, where profit forecasts remain solid," said Kang Dae-seung, an analyst at SK Securities.Share buybacks by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are another factor cushioning the index.
